title: SOX17/ETV2 improves the direct reprogramming of adult fibroblasts to endothelial cells.
model: Adult human dermal fibroblasts; in vivo vessel assay
methods: Factor overexpression; EC marker analysis; Vessel formation
finding: SOX17 combined with ETV2 improved fibroblast conversion and several endothelial functional readouts.
limitation: The abstract covers selected functional assays; it leaves long-term stability across tissue settings unresolved.
evidence_quote: by overexpressing SOX17 in conjunction with ETV2

title: Endothelial Reprogramming by Disturbed Flow Revealed by Single-Cell RNA and Chromatin Accessibility Study.
factors: KLF2; KLF4; RELA; AP1; STAT1; TEAD1
model: Mouse partial carotid ligation
methods: scRNA-seq; scATAC-seq; Pseudotime
finding: Disturbed flow was associated with endothelial inflammatory and mesenchymal programs and altered motif accessibility.
limitation: Pseudotime and motif accessibility suggest changes in cell state; lineage tracing and perturbation would be needed to test the proposed transitions and regulators.
evidence_quote: single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and scATAC-seq

title: Endothelial GATA4 controls liver fibrosis and regeneration by preventing a pathogenic switch in angiocrine signaling.
model: Adult mouse LSEC-specific Gata4 knockout; human cirrhosis datasets
methods: Conditional knockout; ATAC-seq; ChIP-seq; Expression profiling
finding: Loss of endothelial GATA4 induced sinusoidal capillarization and profibrotic signaling involving MYC and PDGFB.
limitation: The mouse knockout tests the effect of GATA4 loss. The human cirrhosis comparison is observational.
evidence_quote: LSEC-to-continuous endothelial transdifferentiation

title: Venous Endothelial Marker COUP-TFII Regulates the Distinct Pathologic Potentials of Adult Arteries and Veins.
model: Adult venous endothelial cultures; mouse artery/vein comparison
methods: Knockdown; Overexpression; Gene expression
finding: COUP-TFII manipulation changed inflammatory, thrombotic and mesenchymal phenotypes of venous endothelial cells.
limitation: COUP-TFII accounts for part of a broader set of differences between arteries and veins.
evidence_quote: COUP-TFII knockdown also readily undergo endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition

title: ETV2 Upregulation Marks the Specification of Early Cardiomyocytes and Endothelial Cells During Co-differentiation.
model: Human iPSC cardiac/endothelial co-differentiation
methods: scRNA-seq; Fluorescent reporter
finding: ETV2 expression dynamics distinguished early endothelial and cardiomyocyte lineage-predisposed states.
limitation: These reporter dynamics come from an in vitro differentiation system. Their relevance to development in vivo needs testing.
evidence_quote: a transient ETV2-high-state initiates the specification of endothelial cells

title: ETV2 functions as a pioneer factor to regulate and reprogram the endothelial lineage.
model: Engineered embryonic stem-cell differentiation and reprogramming models
methods: Multi-omics; Chromatin binding; Chromatin remodeling
finding: ETV2 bound nucleosomal DNA and recruited BRG1, linking pioneer activity to endothelial chromatin opening.
limitation: The mechanism comes from engineered differentiation and reprogramming models; its range across endothelial contexts remains a question.
evidence_quote: ETV2 was able to bind nucleosomal DNA and recruit BRG1

title: Production of endothelial progenitor cells from skin fibroblasts by direct reprogramming for clinical usages.
journal: In vitro cellular & developmental biology. Animal
model: Human skin fibroblasts; mouse hindlimb ischemia assay
methods: mRNA transfection; Hypoxia culture; Marker and functional assays
finding: ETV2 mRNA plus hypoxia generated endothelial progenitor-like cells from fibroblasts at low reported efficiency.
limitation: The reported conversion efficiency was low, and the functional test used a mouse ischemia model.
evidence_quote: ETV2 mRNA combined with hypoxia can give rise to functional EPCs

title: Direct conversion of human amniotic cells into endothelial cells without transitioning through a pluripotent state.
model: Human amniotic fluid-derived cells; implantation in mice
methods: Conversion protocol; ETS factor expression; TGF-beta inhibition
finding: A conversion platform combined transient ETV2 with sustained FLI1/ERG1 and TGF-beta inhibition to produce expandable endothelium.
limitation: This paper describes a conversion protocol. Its therapeutic usefulness would need separate testing.
evidence_quote: constitutive expression the ETS transcription factors FLI1 and ERG1

title: Sox17 mediates adult arterial endothelial cell adaptation to hemodynamics.
model: Cultured venous endothelial cells under controlled flow
methods: Inducible expression; 3D fibrin assays; Microfluidics
finding: SOX17 induced arterial/tip-cell programs whose functional effects depended on mechanical and supporting-cell context.
limitation: Cultured venous cells under controlled flow capture only part of the environment in adult arteries.
evidence_quote: Sox17-induced ECs exhibit a gene profile favoring arterial and tip cell identity

title: Overexpression of Prox1 Induces the Differentiation of Human Adipose-Derived Stem Cells into Lymphatic Endothelial-Like Cells In Vitro.
model: Human adipose-derived stem cells in vitro
methods: Lentiviral overexpression; Flow cytometry; RT-PCR; Tube formation
finding: PROX1 overexpression induced lymphatic endothelial-like markers and tube-forming behavior.
limitation: Marker expression and Matrigel tube formation leave mature lymphatic function unresolved.
evidence_quote: induced the differentiation of hADSCs into stable lymphatic endothelial-like cells

title: cAMP/EPAC Signaling Enables ETV2 to Induce Endothelial Cells with High Angiogenesis Potential.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
model: Human fibroblast conversion; vascular functional assays
methods: ChIP-seq; Signaling-modulator screen; Angiogenesis assays
finding: Activation of cAMP/EPAC/RAP1 enhanced ETV2-driven conversion and angiogenesis-related function.
limitation: The assays assess conversion and angiogenesis; broader comparisons with native endothelium would help establish how complete the conversion is.
evidence_quote: forskolin facilitated efficient and rapid iEC reprogramming

title: The pioneer factor, ETV2, regulates networks to specify the embryonic endothelial lineage.
model: Mouse ESC/embryoid bodies and embryos
methods: scRNA-seq; ATAC-seq; ChIP-seq; Knockout; EMSA
finding: ETV2 dosage and context promoted hematoendothelial programs while suppressing alternative mesodermal programs, including Mesp1.
limitation: The experiments use mouse developmental models, which may behave differently from human differentiation cultures.
evidence_quote: Master regulators of the cardiac lineage including Mesp1

title: TWIST1-Reprogrammed Endothelial Cell Transplantation Potentiates Neovascularization-Mediated Diabetic Wound Tissue Regeneration.
model: Wharton jelly stromal cells; diabetic mouse wounds
methods: Expression-data meta-analysis; TF perturbation; Cell transplantation
finding: TWIST1 promoted endothelial programming of stromal cells and vascular repair readouts in diabetic mouse wounds.
limitation: The result depends on the starting stromal cells and experimental setting; TWIST1 can have different roles in other endothelial contexts.
evidence_quote: Twist1 reprogramming enhanced the endothelial lineage commitment of WJ-MSC

title: ETV2 induces endothelial, but not hematopoietic, lineage specification in birds.
model: Chicken mesoderm, gecko and comparative avian genomics
methods: Comparative genomics; Ectopic expression; Epistasis
finding: Ectopic ETV2 induced an endothelial-associated program in avian mesoderm without the corresponding hematopoietic response.
limitation: The ancestral regulatory model is an inference from comparative genomes and expression experiments.
evidence_quote: Mouse ETV2 induced LMO2, but not NPAS4L or SCL

title: Pioneer factor ETV2 safeguards endothelial cell specification by recruiting the repressor REST to restrict alternative lineage commitment.
model: Human iPSC-derived mesodermal progenitors
methods: CUT&RUN; scRNA-seq; scATAC-seq; Functional screening
finding: ETV2 used both activating cofactors and REST-mediated repression of alternative-lineage genes during endothelial specification.
limitation: The experiments use induced differentiation. Whether the same mechanism operates across adult endothelial tissues needs testing.
evidence_quote: ETV2 recruited REST to repress non-EC lineage genes

title: Targeted CRISPR-Cas9 screening identifies core transcription factors controlling murine haemato-endothelial fate commitment.
model: Murine embryonic stem-cell model of embryonic blood development
methods: Targeted CRISPR knockout screen; Transcriptome analysis
finding: A targeted screen identified regulators whose loss biased mesoderm away from normal haemato-endothelial commitment.
limitation: The screen covers selected transcription factors and chromatin regulators in a mouse cell model.
evidence_quote: ETV2, LDB1, SMAD1, SIX4 and ZBTB7b

title: HOXB4 Promotes Hemogenic Endothelium Formation without Perturbing Endothelial Cell Development.
model: Differentiating mouse ESCs with inducible Runx1
methods: Retroviral expression; Inducible rescue; Transcriptome analysis
finding: HOXB4 promoted hemogenic endothelium formation while preserving overall endothelial development.
limitation: The endpoint is hemogenic endothelium, a developmental state distinct from mature vascular endothelium.
evidence_quote: HOXB4 promoted the formation of hemogenic endothelium cells

title: Cardiac endothelial cells maintain open chromatin and expression of cardiomyocyte myofibrillar genes.
model: Cardiac endothelial cells and isolated nuclei
methods: Bulk RNA-seq; scRNA-seq; In situ hybridization; ATAC-seq
finding: Cardiac endothelial cells showed cell-autonomous myofibrillar transcription and promoter accessibility that diminished in culture.
limitation: Motif enrichment points to possible regulators, but the abstract does not establish a causal role for an individual factor.
evidence_quote: have open chromatin at CMF gene promoters

title: Transcription factor 4 maintains endothelial cell identity by inhibiting endothelial to mesenchymal transition.
model: Endothelial cultures, EndoMT models and heart-failure patient ECs
methods: Knockdown; Promoter binding; Exogenous expression
finding: TCF4 repressed TGF-beta-pathway genes and helped maintain endothelial phenotype against EndoMT.
limitation: TCF4 refers to ITF2 in this paper. The rescue experiments do not establish a treatment effect in patients.
evidence_quote: TCF4; also known as ITF2

title: Unraveling the transcriptional determinants of liver sinusoidal endothelial cell specialization.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
model: Liver/heart/brain EC comparison and engineered HUVECs
methods: Comparative expression; TF overexpression; Protein assays
finding: C-MAF, GATA4 and MEIS2 together increased a liver-sinusoidal marker program but did not fully recreate LSEC function.
limitation: The three-factor combination did not significantly induce receptor-mediated endocytosis, leaving an important LSEC function incomplete.
evidence_quote: receptor-mediated endocytosis was not significantly induced

title: Vegf signaling promotes vascular endothelial differentiation by modulating etv2 expression.
model: Zebrafish embryos
methods: VEGFR inhibition; Genetic mutants; Overexpression rescue
finding: VEGF signaling levels influenced general endothelial differentiation and arterial specification, partly through etv2.
limitation: Both dose and developmental timing affect the result, and broad VEGFR inhibition also affects cell survival.
evidence_quote: Vegf signaling affects overall endothelial differentiation

title: ERG preserves endothelial identity to limit atherosclerosis.
model: Hypercholesterolemic mice, human plaques and cultured EndMT cells
methods: Inducible knockout; Lineage tracing; Single-cell transcriptomics; Restoration
finding: ERG loss promoted endothelial identity loss and atherosclerotic pathology; restoration reversed mesenchymal programs in culture.
limitation: The human plaque comparisons are observational. The restoration experiment tests cultured cells.
evidence_quote: ERG loss drove endothelial dedifferentiation

title: SOX9 reprograms endothelial cells by altering the chromatin landscape.
model: HUVEC EndMT model; atherosclerotic lesions
methods: Factor expression; Chromatin profiling; Single-cell accessibility
finding: SOX9 altered endothelial chromatin and induced persistent mesenchymal programs despite dynamic factor binding.
limitation: SOX9 was sufficient to drive changes in the tested setting, but its contribution relative to other EndMT regulators remains open.
evidence_quote: SOX9 expression alone is sufficient to activate mesenchymal genes

title: Endothelial c-Maf prevents MASLD-like liver fibrosis by regulating chromatin accessibility to suppress pathogenic microvascular cell subsets.
model: LSEC-specific Maf knockout mice and human liver datasets
methods: Conditional knockout; Bulk RNA-seq; ATAC-seq; scRNA-seq
finding: Endothelial c-Maf loss disrupted sinusoidal differentiation and zonation, with pathogenic endothelial subsets and liver fibrosis.
limitation: The mouse knockout tests c-Maf function; the human cirrhosis data show expression differences.
evidence_quote: a switch from sinusoidal to continuous endothelial cell identity

title: Induction of hematopoietic and endothelial cell program orchestrated by ETS transcription factor ER71/ETV2.
model: Mouse ESC differentiation and germline/conditional knockout models
methods: Binding-site mapping; In vitro differentiation; Mouse knockout
finding: ETV2 initiated a hemangiogenic regulatory hierarchy that other ETS factors partly maintained after the initial specification phase.
limitation: The abstract leaves the contributions of individual downstream ETS factors only partly resolved.
evidence_quote: an ETS switching mechanism
